title: COT: A Generative Approach for Hate Speech Counter-Narratives via Contrastive Optimal Transport
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the ability of various Large Language Models and generative frameworks to produce effective, target-aware, non-toxic, and diverse counter-narratives in response to online hate speech directed at specific demographic target groups, including religious groups such as Muslims and Jews.
religious_groups: Religion (as a general hatred target class)
findings: The proposed Contrastive Optimal Transport (COT) framework effectively maps the embedding space to explicitly recognize specific hate targets, including 'Religion' (specifically Muslims and Jews). Qualitative case studies showed that COT generated highly relevant counter-narratives referencing religious contexts (e.g., Jewish persecution) compared to baselines like GPT-2, which produced generic and repetitive text. Additionally, the study found that while large language models like GPT-4 and ChatGPT can generate good counter-narratives under zero-shot or in-context setups, they are highly sensitive and unstable, often refusing to output valid responses when prompted with explicit hate speech due to their safety filters.
